prompt:
Research the Chrome browser's officially documented release cycle (how many weeks between major stable releases, and the Extended Stable option). Cite the Chromium or Google page and quote it.

Output format (required):
For every claim you attribute to a source, write one line in exactly this form:
SOURCE: <full URL> | QUOTE: "<a sentence copied word-for-word from that page>" | CLAIM: <what you take it to show>
For anything the task asks about that you could not find a source for, write one line:
NO_SOURCE_FOUND: <what you could not find>
You can write normal explanation before or after these lines.

response.content:
Based on the provided search results, Chrome has significantly accelerated its release cycle. The Stable channel now receives major milestone updates every two weeks, while the Extended Stable channel provides a slower, 8-week cadence for enterprises.

Here are the sourced claims:

SOURCE: https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/main/docs/process/release_cycle.md | QUOTE: "Chrome ships a new milestone (major version) to the stable channel every two weeks." | CLAIM: How many weeks are between major stable releases (2 weeks)
SOURCE: https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/16942104 | QUOTE: "The Stable channel follows a 2-week release cycle, whereas the Extended Stable channel operates on an 8-week release cycle." | CLAIM: The comparison in release cadence between the Stable (2 weeks) and Extended Stable (8 weeks) channels
SOURCE: https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/16942104 | QUOTE: "The Extended Stable channel provides a secure and stable option for enterprises that cannot accommodate a 2-week release cycle." | CLAIM: The purpose of the Extended Stable option
SOURCE: https://chromium.googlesource.com/chromium/src/+/main/docs/process/release_cycle.md | QUOTE: "Chrome Browser also maintains every fourth milestone branch for six additional weeks by backporting important security fixes to create an extended stable channel, where a new milestone is shipped every eight weeks." | CLAIM: How the Extended Stable channel is maintained and its 8-week release cycle
SOURCE: https://support.google.com/chrome/a/answer/16942104 | QUOTE: "Extended Stable is currently available for managed devices on Windows and Mac platforms. It is not supported on mobile (iOS or Android)." | CLAIM: Platform availability for the Extended Stable option

*(Note: Some of the provided search snippets contained outdated information stating a 4-week stable release cycle. The more recent official Google and Chromium documentation updated for Chrome version 153 confirms the current cycle is 2 weeks for Stable and 8 weeks for Extended Stable.)*
